title: HERMES.md in commit messages causes Anthropic API billing routing
description: Hacker News discussion (983 points) revealed that including 'HERMES.md' in commit messages triggers requests to route to Anthropic's extra usage billing tier. Anthropic GitHub documentation explains HERMES is their internal request format. Community concern: (1) Lack of transparency about automatic routing triggers; (2) Developers unaware of billing implications; (3) Questions about whether other patterns trigger premium routing. Discussion highlights growing complexity of AI API pricing models and need for clear documentation about automatic tier selection.
author: Anthropic, discussed on Hacker News

title: Flue - Agent Harness Framework for TypeScript
description: Flue is a TypeScript framework for building autonomous agents with a programmable harness architecture. Not another SDK - write once, deploy anywhere. Key features: (1) Agent = Model + Harness architecture similar to Claude Code and Codex; (2) Skills as reusable workflows with structured output using valibot schemas; (3) Session management like Claude Code with prompt tracking; (4) Fine-grained control over sensitive tokens and API keys; (5) Support for multiple sandboxes: virtual (zero-config), Daytona containers, Cloudflare Workers with R2; (6) Can deploy as HTTP server or run from CLI for local tasks and CI; (7) Built-in virtualization for filesystem operations - agents use read/write/grep tools regardless of whether target is local or remote. Philosophy: 'Stop renting someone else's agent' - build your own AI issue triage in 22 lines of TypeScript. Replaces Dosu, Greptile, CodeRabbit with owned stack.
author: Flue Team

title: The Agent Harness Belongs Outside the Sandbox
description: Mendral argues that agent harnesses (the LLM loop) should run outside the sandbox, not inside. Architecture comparison: Inside (Claude Code local model) = loop lives in same container, simple execution, off-the-shelf harnesses work. Outside (Mendral's choice) = loop runs on backend, calls into sandbox over API. Tradeoffs of outside model: (1) Credentials stay out of sandbox - loop holds API keys, sandbox holds only workspace; (2) Can suspend sandbox when idle - saves cost, most agent work (thinking, API calls) doesn't need sandbox; (3) Sandboxes become cattle - if one dies, loop provisions new one and continues; (4) Multi-user becomes database problem, not distributed filesystem problem. Three problems solved: (1) Durable execution with Inngest for long-running sessions; (2) Sandbox lifecycle with Blaxel for 25ms resume from standby; (3) Filesystem virtualization - one interface (read/write/edit) routes workspace paths to sandbox, skill/memory paths to database. Key insight: Virtualized interface keeps API surface that models were trained on while adding database semantics where needed. Challenge: Bash is a leak - agents can run grep on /skills/ which bypasses virtualization.
author: Mendral

title: VS Code inserting 'Co-Authored-by Copilot' into commits regardless of usage
description: Microsoft VS Code PR #310226 changed git.addAICoAuthor setting default from 'off' to 'all', automatically adding 'Co-authored-by: Copilot <copilot@github.com>' trailer to commits when AI-generated code is detected. Community backlash: 129 thumbs down, 18 confused reactions. Issues: (1) Inserts even when users have 'chat.disableAIFeatures': true; (2) Inserts even when Copilot wasn't used for that commit; (3) Silent default with no user notification; (4) Conflates 'used editor' with 'co-authored', degrading Co-Authored-by signal; (5) Users call it 'vandalism' and question whether Copilot adoption metrics are being inflated. Comparisons: Cursor handles this differently - no automatic attribution, workflow assumes diff review, author is whoever ran git commit. Revert PR opened (#313725). Some users switching to Zed 1.0 which has single option to disable all AI features globally.
author: Microsoft VS Code Team

title: The best AI dictation apps, tested and ranked
description: TechCrunch comprehensive review of AI-powered dictation apps highlighting advances in LLMs and speech-to-text models that enable more accurate transcription with better formatting, automatic filler word removal, and punctuation handling. Notable apps: (1) Wispr Flow - well-funded, customizable dictation with vibe-coding integration for Cursor to recognize variables and tag files; (2) Willow - privacy-focused with local storage and custom vocabulary; (3) Monologue - downloadable AI model for fully offline use; (4) Superwhisper - supports multiple AI models including Parakeet, translation features; (5) VoiceTypr - offline-first, no-subscription, open source; (6) Aqua - YC-backed, claims fast latency with autofill phrases; (7) Typeless - highest free tier at 4,000 words/week; (8) Dictato - €9.99 lifetime with 80ms latency using offline models. Pricing models vary from $8-15/month subscriptions to $35-100+ lifetime licenses. The article notes these apps are useful for 'even coding through your voice' when integrated with IDE tools.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Show HN: State of the Art of Coding Models, According to Hacker News Commenters
description: Hacker News discussion thread aggregating community opinions on the state-of-the-art coding models based on commenter experiences and benchmarks. Discussion covers various models' performance on coding tasks, with contributors sharing real-world usage patterns and comparative analysis.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Who owns the code Claude Code wrote? - Legal Ownership Debate
description: Hacker News discussion (539 points) sparked by article questioning AI-generated code ownership. Boris Cherny, Anthropic lead engineer and Claude Code creator, stated that 100% of his recent contributions to Claude Code were written by the AI itself. Earlier reports indicate 80-90% of Claude Code's codebase was AI-generated. Legal questions: (1) If Claude Code wrote itself, does Anthropic own it? Ownership likely stems from employment contracts rather than creation act; (2) What about code Claude writes for users? Anthropic's ToS states users retain ownership of outputs, but copyright law requires human authorship; (3) AI-generated code may not be protectable under current copyright frameworks. Discussion highlights growing legal ambiguity as AI tools become more autonomous. Community concern: 'The legal mess no one's talking about' could become significant business risk.
author: Legal Layer Substack, discussed on Hacker News

title: Musk v. Altman week 1: Elon Musk admits xAI distills OpenAI's models
description: Week 1 of the landmark trial between Elon Musk and OpenAI featured dramatic testimony. Key revelations: (1) Musk testified he was 'a fool who provided them free funding' of $38 million to create what became an $800B company; (2) Musk warned 'The worst-case scenario is a Terminator situation where AI kills us all'; (3) Under cross-examination, Musk admitted xAI 'partly' distills OpenAI's models - using OpenAI's technology to train Grok, causing audible gasps in the courtroom; (4) OpenAI lawyer William Savitt argued Musk is suing to undermine a competitor, noting Musk hired away OpenAI cofounder Andrej Karpathy in 2017; (5) Musk's attorney argued xAI is 'not currently tracking to reach AGI first' to downplay competitive threat; (6) Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers pushed back on the trial becoming about AI safety: 'I suspect there's plenty of people who don't want to put the future of humanity in Mr. Musk's hands.' The trial's outcome could upend OpenAI's path to a $1T IPO. xAI expected to go public via SpaceX in June at $1.75T valuation.
author: Michelle T. Kim, MIT Technology Review

title: OpenAI Enables Marketing Cookies by Default for Free ChatGPT Users
description: OpenAI updated its privacy policy to enable marketing cookies by default for free ChatGPT users in the US. The company now uses cookies to track users across the web and promote OpenAI products on third-party websites. Key changes: (1) Marketing cookies set to 'on' by default for free users (paying Plus/Enterprise users not affected); (2) OpenAI shares limited identifiers (email, cookie IDs, device IDs) with advertising partners to track ad conversions; (3) Chats with ChatGPT remain private and are not shared with marketing partners; (4) Users can opt out via Settings > Data Controls > Marketing Privacy. The policy change reveals OpenAI's strategy to convert free users to paying subscribers through targeted advertising, similar to Google's approach of weaving ads into generative AI tools. WIRED verified the default-on behavior by testing two free accounts.
author: Reece Rogers, Maddy Varner

title: Meta buys robotics startup to bolster its humanoid AI ambitions
description: Meta acquired humanoid robotics startup Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI) for an undisclosed sum. The ARI team including co-founders Lerrel Pinto (NYU, Fauna Robotics) and Xiaolong Wang (Nvidia, UCSD) will join Meta's Superintelligence Labs research division. ARI was building foundation models for humanoid robots to perform physical labor like household chores. This reflects Meta's long-term humanoid robotics ambitions (leaked memo from a year ago discussed building AI models and hardware for consumers). Industry context: Forecasts for humanoid robotics market vary wildly from Goldman Sachs' $38B by 2035 to Morgan Stanley's $5T by 2050. The ARI acquisition follows Amazon's acquisition of Fauna Robotics last month, reflecting broader industry investment in robotics as a path to AGI through physical world training.
author: Julie Bort

title: Goodfire's Silico: Mechanistic Interpretability Tool to Debug LLMs
description: Goodfire released Silico, a mechanistic interpretability tool that lets developers debug and tweak LLMs by examining individual neurons and pathways. The company aims to make training AI models 'less like alchemy and more like a science' by exposing the internal knobs and dials of model behavior. Key features: (1) Zoom in on specific neurons or groups of neurons in trained models; (2) Run experiments to see what inputs make different neurons fire; (3) Trace pathways upstream and downstream to understand neural interactions; (4) Adjust parameters connected to individual neurons to boost or suppress behaviors; (5) Filter training data to avoid setting unwanted values during training. Real-world examples: Found a 'trolley problem' neuron in Qwen 3 that frames outputs as moral dilemmas when activated; Boosted transparency/disclosure neurons to flip a model's answer from 'no' to 'yes' (9/10 times) on whether a company should disclose deceptive AI behavior. Tool uses agents to automate interpretability work previously done by humans. Available for fee based on customer requirements. Targets smaller firms and research teams that can't afford in-house interpretability researchers.
author: Will Douglas Heaven

title: Codex CLI 0.128.0 adds /goal feature
description: OpenAI's Codex CLI version 0.128.0 introduces a /goal feature, similar to the Ralph loop pattern. Users can now set a goal and Codex will continue looping until it evaluates that the goal has been completed or the configured token budget is exhausted. The feature is implemented through prompts in goals/continuation.md and goals/budget_limit.md which are automatically injected at the end of each turn, enabling autonomous iterative problem-solving within set token limits.
author: Simon Willison (linking to OpenAI)

title: Andrej Karpathy on Software 3.0 and 'Vibe Coding' at Sequoia AI Ascent 2026
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Andrej Karpathy outlined three-stage evolution of software: Software 1.0 (explicit rules), Software 2.0 (data + neural networks), Software 3.0 (context + prompts, letting LLMs handle intelligence). He popularized 'vibe coding' - programming primarily through AI tools like Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Key insights: (1) English becoming primary programming language, not Python/Java/C++; (2) Shift from 80% manual coding + 20% AI to AI-dominant workflow; (3) 'Starting to atrophy' ability to write code manually; (4) Predicts 2026 will be 'Slopacolypse' - potential issues with AI-generated content quality. Discussion of three types of programmers emerging in 2026 landscape. Called 'one of the most important AI talks of the year' reflecting on one-year anniversary of coding trend that changed tech industry.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: LLM 0.32a0 is a major backwards-compatible refactor
description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.32a0, a major alpha release of his LLM Python library and CLI tool. Key changes: (1) Model inputs now represented as sequence of messages instead of simple prompts, supporting conversation history and multi-turn exchanges; (2) Model responses can now be composed of streams of differently typed parts (text, tool calls, reasoning, images, audio). The new API supports streaming typed message parts, making it easier to handle modern frontier models that return mixed content types including reasoning, tool calls, and multi-modal outputs. Added builder functions like user() and assistant() and response.reply() methods. CLI gains -R/--no-reasoning flag and thinking_display option for colored reasoning output.
author: Simon Willison

title: Zed 1.0 Released - High-Performance AI-Native Code Editor
description: Zed Industries released Zed 1.0, a high-performance, multiplayer code editor built from scratch in Rust. Key features: (1) Agentic editing - native support for AI agents including Claude Agent, Codex, and OpenCode via ACP; (2) Parallel Agents - run multiple AI agents simultaneously across projects; (3) Edit Prediction powered by Zeta2, their open-weight language model; (4) Built-in collaboration for real-time coding with teammates; (5) GPU-accelerated rendering for exceptional performance. The editor emphasizes 'fluent collaboration between humans and AI' with native MCP server support. Notable endorsements from José Valim (Elixir creator), Ethan Perez (Adversarial Robustness Research Lead), Dan Abramov (React Core Team), and Mike Bostock (D3.js creator). Zed 1.0 represents the culmination of 15 years of work from the creators of Atom, Electron, and Tree-sitter.
author: Nathan Sobo, Zed Industries

title: Microsoft VibeVoice - Whisper-style audio model
description: Microsoft released VibeVoice, a Whisper-style audio model for speech-to-text with speaker diarization built in. MIT licensed. Released January 21, 2026 but highlighted by Simon Willison on April 27, 2026. Model is 17.3GB, with 4-bit quantized version at 5.71GB available. Can run on Apple Silicon using mlx-audio with a simple one-liner command using uv package manager.
author: Simon Willison

title: Tracking the history of the now-deceased OpenAI Microsoft AGI clause
description: Simon Willison documents the death of the unusual AGI clause in the Microsoft-OpenAI partnership. Originally, the clause stated that Microsoft's commercial IP rights to OpenAI technology would end upon AGI achievement. The definition evolved from 'highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work' (2018) to systems capable of generating $100B in profit (reported Dec 2024) to being judged by an independent expert panel (Oct 2025). As of April 27, 2026, the new partnership agreement states Microsoft's license continues through 2032 'independent of OpenAI's technology progress' - effectively killing the AGI escape clause. Includes Matt Levine's 2023 hypothetical about benign ASI ending capitalism.
author: Simon Willison

title: VibeVoice: Microsoft's Open-Source Frontier Voice AI
description: Microsoft open-sourced VibeVoice, a family of frontier voice AI models including both Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Key innovations: (1) Continuous speech tokenizers (Acoustic and Semantic) at ultra-low 7.5 Hz frame rate; (2) VibeVoice-ASR handles 60-minute long-form audio in single pass with speaker diarization, timestamps, and customized hotwords; (3) VibeVoice-TTS synthesizes 90-minute conversational audio with up to 4 distinct speakers; (4) Real-time streaming TTS model (0.5B) with ~300ms latency; (5) MIT licensed, supports 50+ languages natively; (6) vLLM inference support for faster processing. Notable: VibeVoice-TTS code was removed Sept 2025 after discovering misuse inconsistent with stated intent. Hugging Face Transformers integration added March 2026. Available as 17.3GB model with 5.71GB 4-bit quantized version for Apple Silicon via mlx-audio.
author: Microsoft
